mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the last two months signals a decline in demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts dropped by more than 10% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months signals a potential for continued accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real interest rates remain low.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals increased consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings benefit from higher sales.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tight labor market with restrictive monetary policy, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the cost of capital increases and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and UNRATE was below 4%.
